union.summary: Blank-cell skipping in `Arguments.iterate` is a sweeping behavior change for ALL ranges (not just unbounded ones), but is only exercised incidentally by one AVERAGE and one COUNT case; MIN/MAX/PRODUCT/AND/OR/CONCAT over ranges containing blanks get no test at all
union.evidence: arguments.ts (diff hunk at ~line 108-125) now `continue`s over any cell in a *range* whose `v` is undefined/'' — this applies to every `Arguments.iterate` consumer: sumFunc, productFunc, gcdFunc/lcmFunc, sumsqFunc, averageFunc, medianFunc, minFunc, maxFunc, stdev/var/mode/geomean (grep `\.iterate\(` in packages/sheets/src/formula/functions-*.ts), plus BoolArgs (AND/OR) and StringArgs (CONCAT). Previously a blank cell in a bounded range yielded 0/''/false; now it is dropped. The only tests added are the unbounded-range ones: test/sheet/calculation.test.ts `=AVERAGE(B2:B)` → 200 and `=COUNT(A:B)` → 5, and test/formula/formula.test.ts 'Unbounded ranges'. Nothing asserts the new semantics for a plain bounded range (`=AVERAGE(A1:A3)` with A2 blank), for `=PRODUCT(A1:A3)` (a blank used to zero the product, now it doesn't), or for MIN/MAX where the accumulator is seeded with ±Infinity (functions-statistical.ts minFunc `let result = Infinity` / maxFunc `-Infinity`) so an all-blank range can now leak 'Infinity' instead of a number. I searched test/formula/formula.test.ts for AVERAGE/MIN/MAX/COUNT range cases: all existing grids are fully populated or use text (e.g. AVERAGEA at line 2026), so no pre-existing test pins this behavior either.

union.summary: `expandUnboundedRanges` reconstructs the whole formula string from tokens, but every test that reaches the rebuild path is a single-function/single-reference formula — mixed formulas, string literals and whitespace are untested
union.evidence: formula.ts `expandUnboundedRanges` builds `'=' + body` by concatenating every token's text (including the synthetic STRING gap tokens produced by `extractTokens`). Corruption of any surrounding text would silently rewrite user formulas. The added tests (test/formula/formula.test.ts 'Unbounded ranges') only pass `=SUM(A:A)`, `=SUM(1:1)`, `=AVERAGE(B2:B)`, `=COUNT(A:B)`, `=SUM(1:3)` — all single-call/single-ref. The 'leaves bounded formulas untouched' test (`=SUM(A1:B2)`, `=A1+B2`, `hello`) returns via the early `!tokens.some(shouldExpand)` fast path, so it does not exercise the rebuild at all. No test covers e.g. `=SUM(A:A)+B1*2`, `=COUNT(1:1)&" rows"`, `=SUM( A:A )` with spaces, or a string literal containing ':'.

union.summary: New `CellIndex.bounds()` has no unit test; the `undefined` (empty index) branch is not covered end-to-end and the 'otherwise empty sheet' calculation test does not actually produce undefined bounds
union.evidence: The diff adds `CellIndex.bounds()` (cell-index.ts) but does not touch packages/sheets/test/store/cell-index.test.ts — that file has describes only for cellsInRange, hasAnyInRange, getOccupiedColsInRow/getOccupiedRowsInCol (no `bounds`). Its distinctive logic (min/max row from rowIndex and min/max col from colIndex computed independently, so bounds may include never-populated cells) is untested. test/sheet/calculation.test.ts 'evaluates a whole-column reference on an otherwise empty sheet' writes `=SUM(A:A)` into D1, so the index is non-empty and bounds() returns [{1,4},{1,4}] — the `undefined` return is only ever hit by the unit test that passes `undefined` directly to expandUnboundedRanges, never through a store.

union.summary: `resolveRange` tests only use bounds starting at {r:1,c:1}, so the assertions hold whether omitted endpoints default to row1/col1 or to the bounds minimum
union.evidence: All resolveRange cases use `const bounds = r(1, 1, 3, 2)`. For `A:A`, `1:1`, `A1:B`, `A:B2` the expected results are identical under the implemented rule (`a.r ?? 1`, `a.c ?? 1`) and under the plausible alternative (`?? bounds[0].r/c`), so the documented 'from omitted → 1/1' behavior is not actually pinned. No case uses a data extent that does not start at A1 (e.g. bounds [{5,3},{8,4}]). Same gap in test/sheet/calculation.test.ts, where the seed always starts at A1.

union.summary: YorkieStore's three `buildDependantsMap` rewrite sites and `getUsedBounds`, plus `ReadOnlyStore.getUsedBounds`, ship with no test
union.evidence: The diff wires `expandUnboundedRanges` into three separate loops in YorkieStore.buildDependantsMap (document entries, batch overlay, and the cache/fallback loop) and adds `getUsedBounds()`, but adds no test. Grepping packages/frontend for `A:A`/`1:1`/`getUsedBounds` finds only the source line yorkie-store.ts:614 — none of the existing yorkie spreadsheet tests (tests/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-concurrency.test.ts etc.) exercise unbounded ranges, so the collaborative-store reactivity path claimed in docs/design/sheets/formula.md is unverified. ReadOnlyStore.getUsedBounds (packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts) is likewise untested.

union.summary: Documented limitation 'cross-sheet unbounded refs evaluate to #ERROR!' is never tested end-to-end
union.evidence: docs/design/sheets/formula.md (added in this diff) states `Sheet2!A:A` is not resolved and evaluates to `#ERROR!`. The only related test asserts the pass-through of the *string* (`expandUnboundedRanges('=SUM(Sheet2!A:A)', bounds)` → unchanged) in test/formula/formula.test.ts. No test in test/sheet/cross-sheet-calculation.test.ts or calculation.test.ts asserts what a cell containing `=SUM(Sheet2!A:A)` actually displays, so a crash or a silently wrong number would not be caught.

union.summary: Lexer change makes `A:A`/`1:1` valid REFERENCE tokens, changing the input space of `extractTokens`/`extractFormulaRanges` (highlighting) with no test in this diff
union.evidence: REFRANGE now matches COL:COL / ROW:ROW / REF:COL etc., so `extractFormulaRanges('=SUM(A:A)')` now receives a REFERENCE token that `parseRange` cannot parse and is swallowed by the `catch`. docs/design/sheets/formula.md asserts 'Whole-column/row highlighting (extractFormulaRanges) skips unbounded refs', but the diff adds no assertion (e.g. `expect(extractFormulaRanges('=AVERAGE(B2:B)')).toEqual([])`) and no extractTokens case for the new token shapes, so silent breakage of formula-range highlighting would go unnoticed.

union.summary: No test for a whole-column/row formula that includes its own cell (circular case created by expansion)
union.evidence: Every added calculation test parks the formula in column D at rows outside the referenced row (`=SUM(A:A)` at r1c4, `=SUM(1:1)` at r2c4, `=SUM(1:3)` at r5c4), so the expansion never covers the formula cell itself. Since bounds include the formula cell, `=SUM(A:A)` written into column A (or `=SUM(1:1)` written into row 1) expands to a range containing itself — a new self-reference/cycle path with no coverage.

union.summary: Untested branches in the new coordinate helpers: `isUnboundedRange`'s cross-sheet path and `expandUnboundedRanges`' try/catch fallback
union.evidence: `isUnboundedRange` special-cases cross-sheet refs via `parseCrossSheetRef(...).localRef`, but coordinates.test.ts only passes local refs ('A:A' … '$A:$A', 'A1:B2', 'A1', 'A'); no case like `isUnboundedRange("Sheet2!A:A")`. Similarly the `catch` in expandUnboundedRanges ('Fall through to the original text on any parse failure') has no test input that triggers it.

union.summary: The blank-cell-skipping change in `Arguments.iterate` (a semantic change to every range aggregation, not just unbounded ranges) has no direct test; its stated single-cell exception is untested.
union.evidence: The diff adds `const isRange = isSrng(node.v)` and skips refs whose cell is missing/`v === undefined`/`v === ''` inside ranges. This changes results for ordinary bounded ranges too (e.g. `=AVERAGE(A1:A3)` with A2 blank, `=MIN(A1:A3)` with a blank, `=COUNT`), yet no test in the diff exercises a bounded range containing a blank. The comment claims "A single-cell reference is still yielded as-is so `=SUM(A1)` on a blank A1 stays 0" — no test asserts that branch, so the `isRange` guard could be removed and every added test would still pass. Only incidental coverage exists: `=AVERAGE(B2:B)` → 200 in packages/sheets/test/sheet/calculation.test.ts would be 100 without skipping; `=COUNT(A:B)` → 5 passes either way. No MIN/MAX-over-blanks test at all.

union.summary: Grammar now lexes `A:A`/`1:1`/`A1:B` as REFERENCE tokens, but the non-calculator consumers of those tokens (extractFormulaRanges highlighting, shiftFormula on row/col insert, normalizeFormulaOnCommit, autofill) have no test with an unbounded ref.
union.evidence: docs/design/sheets/formula.md (added text) asserts "Whole-column/row highlighting (`extractFormulaRanges`) skips unbounded refs", but the diff contains no change to `extractFormulaRanges` and no test such as `extractFormulaRanges('=SUM(A:A)')`. `extractFormulaRanges` is documented as parsing every REFERENCE token via `parseRange`, which now receives endpoints like `A` / `1` — behavior (skip vs. throw) is entirely unasserted. Likewise no test inserts/deletes a row or column, or commits/autofills, on a sheet containing `=SUM(A:A)` to check `shiftFormula`/`normalizeFormulaOnCommit` handling of the new token shape.

union.summary: YorkieStore changes (new `getUsedBounds`, `ensureIndex()` in `buildDependantsMap`, and three separate `expandUnboundedRanges` rewrites including the batchOverlay paths) ship with no test in the diff.
union.evidence: The diff modifies three loops in `YorkieStore.buildDependantsMap` (document-entries, batchOverlay-entries, and the trailing loop) plus adds `getUsedBounds()`, but the only reactivity/dependants tests added are packages/sheets/test/sheet/calculation.test.ts using `new Sheet(new MemStore())`. No frontend test in the diff exercises the Yorkie path, so a wrong bounds source, a missed rewrite in the overlay branch, or a missing `ensureIndex()` would not fail any added test. I could not inspect the working tree to confirm whether pre-existing yorkie-store tests cover it.

union.summary: `CellIndex.bounds()` has no direct unit test, and its `undefined` (empty index) return is never exercised end to end.
union.evidence: The diff adds `bounds()` (min/max over `rowIndex` and `colIndex` independently) with no accompanying cell-index test. The "evaluates a whole-column reference on an otherwise empty sheet" test in packages/sheets/test/sheet/calculation.test.ts writes the formula into D1 first, so the index is non-empty and `bounds()` returns a defined range — the `rowIndex.size === 0 → undefined` branch is only covered by passing `undefined` literally to `expandUnboundedRanges` in packages/sheets/test/formula/formula.test.ts. No test covers a bounding box whose min row and min column come from different cells (e.g. B1 and A5).

union.summary: All `resolveRange` tests use bounds anchored at (1,1), so the deliberate decision to default omitted `from` parts to 1/1 rather than to the bounds' minimum is not distinguished by any assertion.

With min = (1,1), a variant implementation using `bounds[0]` for the omitted `from` parts would produce identical results, so the tests cannot fail on that behavior. No case such as bounds `[{r:2,c:2},{r:5,c:5}]` with `A:A`.

union.summary: Several newly-accepted grammar alternatives and case/absolute forms are never lexed or expanded in a test.
union.evidence: The added `extractReferences` test covers only `A:A`, `1:1`, `B2:B`, `A:B`, `1:3`. The grammar adds `COL ':' REF` (`A:B2`), `REF ':' ROW` (`A1:2`), and `ROW ':' REF` (`1:B2`) — none are lexed in a test (only `isUnboundedRange('A:B2')`/`resolveRange('A:B2')` at the coordinates level, which bypass the lexer). Absolute forms (`$A:$A`) and lowercase input (`=sum(a:a)`, which exercises the `token.text.toUpperCase()` path in `expandUnboundedRanges`) are also untested.

union.summary: `expandUnboundedRanges` formula reconstruction (re-joining all tokens, including gap-filled STRING tokens) is only tested on single-reference formulas; the try/catch fallback is untested.
union.evidence: The rewrite loop rebuilds the formula as `'=' + concat(token.text)`. Added tests only use formulas with one unbounded ref and no string literals/whitespace (`=SUM(A:A)`, `=AVERAGE(B2:B)`, ...). No test on e.g. `=SUM(A:A)+SUM(1:1)`, `=SUM(A:A) & "a:b"`, or a formula with spaces, so token-gap-fill / ordering regressions in reconstruction would go undetected. The `catch { fall through }` branch also has no test.

union.summary: Expansion silently drops `$` absolute anchors, and no test pins that behavior.

No test asserts the expanded output for any `$`-anchored unbounded range; `coordinates.test.ts` only asserts `isUnboundedRange('$A:$A') === true`.

union.summary: Documented limitation "cross-sheet unbounded refs evaluate to #ERROR!" and `isUnboundedRange`'s cross-sheet branch are untested.
